title: Ranges of a sorted concurrent set

blocks.text: The page's `ConcurrentSkipListSet` is a thread-safe **sorted** set: it always iterates in sorted order, whatever order the elements arrived in, and it supports `NavigableSet` range operations such as `subSet`, `headSet` and `tailSet`, `first` and `last`. Note that those range operations return **views** backed by the set, and that `subSet`'s bounds can each be inclusive or not.

items: `Ranks.between(set, from, to)` returns, as a **new** sorted set that later changes to the set do not affect, the names `n` with `from <= n <= to`, in sorted order. Both bounds are **inclusive**. Order is `String`'s natural order, which is case-sensitive: `"Banana"` sorts before `"apple"`.
`Ranks.ends(set)` returns `[first, last]`, or an empty list when the set is empty, and leaves the set as it was.

cases.says: between returns the names from the lower bound up to the upper bound in sorted order, and ends names the first and last name.
A name equal to the upper bound is part of the range.
ends of an empty set is an empty list instead of an exception, and ends never removes anything from the set.
The returned range is a copy: names added to the set afterwards do not appear in it.
Names sort in String's natural, case-sensitive order: "Banana" and "Date" come before "apple", in ranges and at the ends.
Each call to between returns a set of its own: a later call does not change an earlier answer.

concepts: ConcurrentSkipListSet keeps its elements sorted and answers first, last and range queries whose bounds can be inclusive, returning views backed by the set.
